text:
maria: Heads-up: we have a support ticket from Tenant-42. They want a per-tenant allowlist override so traffic with their header goes directly to Dedicated pool. Current policy says org denylist should block that.

lee: ugh, classic precedence pain. What header are they sending?

maria: `x-tenant-route: tenant=42;route=dedicated`

jonathan: that header format is brittle. we should only parse `x-redwood-route: tenant=42;mode=dedicated` (already documented). this tenant is using an older shim.

sam: do we currently honor per-tenant overrides at the gateway or only in routing service? last I checked, gateway evaluates allow/deny lists first, then calls routing service for model selection.

lee: correct. gateway has a hard denylist check: if org_id in denylist -> reject. We added allowlist checks for gp-tier earlier but per-tenant override wasn't part of that logic.

maria: tenant says their contract includes an "enterprise exception" to bypass shared pools and route to their reserved pool. ops flagged that the denylist is blocking it.

helen: two immediate questions: 1) should a contract-level per-org override be able to bypass denylists? 2) how do we make this auditable and safe?

jonathan: I'd vote that per-org contractual overrides are higher precedence than generic denylists, but only if the override is recorded and locked. i.e. `override: true` + `locked_by: legal` in the org metadata.

sam: agrees with jonathan. also want a UI guard: when console toggles a bypass you must check a confirmation and we write an audit log and email the SRE rotation. :exclamation:

maria: from infra side: implement in gateway routing order: 1) explicit per-org override header (signed) 2) org-level allowlist/denylist 3) route-match rules 4) fallback. That would let tenants present a signed header to force route.

lee: signed header? extra complexity. we already have customer API keys; maybe we can rely on `x-api-key` -> lookup org metadata that contains `routing_override=true`. No need to trust arbitrary headers.

jonathan: yes, do not trust client-supplied override headers unless they're authenticated and linked to the org and present in our DB. So the gateway should check auth first, then consult org metadata. pseudocode:

```
if auth.org.metadata.routing_override == true and auth.org.metadata.override_locked == true:
  route = auth.org.metadata.preferred_route
else:
  apply_standard_policies()
```

sam: +1. Also add a small rate-limit exemption only for Dedicated routing, else we risk noisy neighbors.

helen: UX request: Console would need a small panel under Org Settings -> Routing with: radio: [Default routing, Prefer Dedicated, Force Dedicated], lock icon, last-changed-by, changelog link. Also an API: `PATCH /orgs/:id/routing` that requires `legal` or `sre` role.

maria: good. need to ensure telemetry: we must tag requests routed via override with `routing.override=true` and expose per-route counters in Console and Prometheus.

lee: what about fallback when dedicated capacity is exhausted? tenant expects failover to Hosted or queue. Our SLA says we can fallback to CompatibleDedicatedVariant or Hosted with notice. Should this be opt-in for overrides?

jonathan: defaults safer: overrides can allow fallback if `allow_fallback=true` in org metadata. otherwise respond with 429 + explanation in body. example response: `{"error":"capacity_exhausted","explain":"tenant override active; allow_fallback=false"}`

sam: logging: include reason codes: `OVERRIDE_APPLIED`, `DENYLIST_BLOCKED`, `ROUTE_MATCHED`, `FALLBACK_USED`. Makes postmortems easier.

maria: ops-bot: deploy check: can we ship this as a config change in gateway v2? deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy to gateway-v2 on branch feature/tenant-override at 2026-04-02T02:00Z`

helen: can someone file a tiny RFC? scope: gateway auth check -> org metadata precedence -> console + API -> telemetry event tags -> fallback behavior. I can draft.

jonathan: I'll put up a WIP PR for the gateway code path and unit tests for precedence edgecases (e.g., org override + denylist entry).

lee: cc @sam please add SLA/contract verification step with biz-ops before we flip anything in prod.

sam: will do. I'll also add a short checklist for legal approval in Console flow.

maria: thanks all. Action items: he request RFC (helen), gateway PR (jonathan), console panel mockups (lee), legal sign-off (sam). I'll triage tenant ticket with a temporary manual exception if needed. :thumbsup:
